correctness.rationale: For n>=8, 3<=k<=n-3, partition homogeneous Euclidean harmonic quartics by the set of odd coordinate exponents, whose sizes are 4,2,0 and remain independent under all sample coordinate-sign flips. Four-odd monomials vanish only at k=3. For each odd pair, harmonicity requires 3(a+b)+Σ_ext c=0 and zero evaluation requires a+b+(k-2)c=0 with c constant by fixed-cardinality subset swap, giving one permanent antisymmetric invisible mode and an extra only at n=3k-4. The even evaluation kernel is the n-dimensional span Q_i=x_i⁴-(1/k)x_i²R, because pair-incidence functions are independent on interior k-slices. The Euclidean Laplacian on Q_i has scalar and sum-zero eigenvalues 4(3k-n-2)/k and 2(6k-n-4)/k, producing extra dimensions 1 at n=3k-2 and n-1 at n=6k-4. Sum of mutually independent parity sectors gives displayed full nullity; checked exact scalar eigenvalues, sample boundary parameters and package modular-rank routine design independently. An infinite formula follows from incidence and Laplacian proofs, not finite modular tests.

value.rationale: The hyperoctahedral signed constant-weight orbit is a canonical sample set. Its full quartic harmonic pointwise kernel quantifies exact unidentifiable modes, gives explicit generators, and separates three nontrivial arithmetic resonance strata beyond its permanent C(n,2) blind modes. This is a complete structural sampling classification not implied by mere spherical design strength or an all-band rank statement without extra work.
